title: Dominic and the Debt
premise: Wendell Halloran, a former analyst for the covert consultancy Meridian, has spent seven years buried under four identities since blowing the whistle on a program that trained operatives for dirty work abroad. When a stranger named Ilsa Voss repays a 'favor' Wendell never performed—and demands interest in the form of a job—Wendell realizes someone has reconstructed their old file and is using it as leverage. Forced back into the network's orbit, Wendell discovers the program wasn't shut down after the whistle-blowing; it was privatized, and the debt being collected is really a hunt for the missing ledger that could burn it all. With help from Ilsa, whose own loyalty is a performance, Wendell retrieves the ledger, exposes the buyers, and ends the story by surrendering the fourth name forever—choosing truth over safety, and testifying as Wendell Halloran one last time.
about_author: Noor Underhill is the pen name of a former compliance investigator who spent a decade inside financial firms before turning to fiction. They live in coastal Maine, where they write about people whose secrets have interest rates.

chapters.title: The Fourth Name
chapters.summary: Wendell, living quietly as 'Daniel Reeve' in a coastal town, wakes at 3 a.m. to a knock: a woman named Ilsa Voss with a file Wendell buried seven years ago. She thanks him for a favor he never did and says interest is owed. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: the fragile peace of anonymity shattering in a single night.

chapters.title: Interest Owed
chapters.summary: Ilsa explains she works for a 'benefactor' who wants one meeting; Wendell refuses, but finds his other three identities have been quietly compromised—bank accounts flagged, leases terminated. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: dread hardening into the realization that invisibility was an illusion someone allowed him.

chapters.title: Meridian's Ghost
chapters.summary: Wendell digs into his old whistleblower cache and finds the Meridian training program's records altered—someone has been editing the archive from inside. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: the sick recognition that the machine he exposed never died; it changed owners.

chapters.title: The Collector
chapters.summary: A man called Ansel Crane arrives in town, polite and patient, interviewing Wendell's neighbors under a survey pretext. Wendell watches him work and understands: this is a retrieval specialist. POV: Wendell, with a brief Crane interlude. Emotional beat: being hunted by someone who genuinely believes he's owed something.

chapters.title: Favors Never Given
chapters.summary: Wendell confronts Ilsa, who admits the 'favor' is fabricated—a hook built from his file. But she slips: she knows a detail about the incident that was never in any document. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: suspicion of his only potential ally, and the first crack in her cover.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Holds
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter to Wendell's Meridian years: the training program, the incident in Tallis Province, and the ledger of clients he copied before fleeing. POV: Wendell (past tense). Emotional beat: guilt reframed—the incident wasn't an accident, it was a product demonstration.

chapters.title: The Buyer's List
chapters.summary: Back in the present, Wendell realizes Crane isn't hunting him—he's hunting the ledger's physical copy, and Wendell's compromised identities are pressure, not capture. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: the cold calculus of deciding to fight instead of run.

chapters.title: Safe House Rules
chapters.summary: Wendell and Ilsa form an uneasy alliance in a derelict marina office; she reveals she was trained by Meridian's successor firm, Halcyon Group, and wants out. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: two liars negotiating the terms of trust.

chapters.title: The Successor
chapters.summary: Research montage: Halcyon inherited Meridian's clients, methods, and a board that includes the man who ordered the Tallis demonstration. Wendell maps the network for the first time. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: rage with a direction—the corruption has a face and an org chart.

chapters.title: Crane's Offer
chapters.summary: Crane corners Wendell publicly and makes a courteous offer: hand over the ledger, keep the fourth name, live. Wendell stalls, buying time, but Crane leaves a message—he knows about the marina. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: temptation, then the vertigo of realizing his safe house is already blown.

chapters.title: Loyalty, Priced
chapters.summary: Ilsa reports to her Halcyon handler as ordered, feeding them false ledger locations—double agent by necessity, not conviction. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: loyalty to Wendell vs. survival, and the first time she chooses the truth over the script.

chapters.title: Dead Drop, Live Wire
chapters.summary: A handoff Wendell stages at a rail yard goes wrong; Crane's team takes the decoy and wounds Ilsa's contact, a retired archivist who once helped Wendell flee. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: guilt compounding—the network burns people who help him.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Key
chapters.summary: Dying, the archivist gives Wendell a deposit-box key and a warning: the ledger alone proves nothing without the client payment trail, which sits inside Halcyon's own servers. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: grief converted into a plan.

chapters.title: Inside Halcyon
chapters.summary: Ilsa returns to Halcyon under cover of a routine assignment and begins exfiltrating the payment trail; Wendell, disguised as a contractor, enters the building where he was once trained. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: the uncanny horror of walking your own past as a stranger.

chapters.title: The Training Floor
chapters.summary: Wendell witnesses the successor program in operation—new recruits, new Tallis Provinces being prepared. He copies the client files but trips a silent audit. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: moral clarity arriving too late to be clean; he's now a thief as well as a witness.

chapters.title: Burn Notice
chapters.summary: Crane presents the board with evidence of Ilsa's betrayal; she's given one chance—deliver Wendell and the ledger, or be erased. POV: Ilsa. Emotional beat: the theme of loyalty vs. truth at its sharpest; she must choose what she is.

chapters.title: The Exchange
chapters.summary: Ilsa arranges a handover at a decommissioned ferry terminal, ostensibly delivering Wendell; instead she feeds Crane a poisoned ledger copy while Wendell watches from the gantry. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: trust as a leap made in the dark—and it holds.

chapters.title: Crane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Crane discovers the forgery, but the real ledger's contents begin leaking to three journalists simultaneously; the board turns on Crane as the leak's obvious weak point. POV: Crane. Emotional beat: the hunter learning he was always expendable inventory.

chapters.title: What Power Owes
chapters.summary: The Halcyon board's fixer comes for Wendell and Ilsa personally; a brutal chase through the marina district ends with Wendell using his knowledge of the program's own protocols against its enforcer. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: the trained turning the training against the trainer.

chapters.title: The Long Night
chapters.summary: Wounded and cornered in a safehouse, Wendell and Ilsa spend the night before publication verifying every page—no errors, no mercy for themselves. Wendell sleeps for the first time in seven years. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: peace found not in safety but in certainty.

chapters.title: Publication Day
chapters.summary: The ledger and payment trail break across three outlets; arrests begin, Halcyon's board scatters, and Crane—offered immunity—hands over everything to save himself. POV: Wendell, watching from a courthouse steps. Emotional beat: vindication that feels less like triumph than like putting down weight.

chapters.title: Wendell Halloran
chapters.summary: Wendell testifies under his real name, retires the other three identities, and meets Ilsa at the marina—both of them, finally, owing nothing. He sleeps through the night. POV: Wendell. Emotional beat: inheritance reclaimed—not the network's legacy, but his own name.
